title: An unconfirmed tail keeps the confirmed row and a damaged complete record is refused
requirement: REQ-294: confirmed board changes survive an interrupted write and the close does not let manual edits through. AC-2: with an incomplete last record the confirmed record stays whole; after a restart the last confirmed row is visible through the service, a repeated allowed change is saved and reopening sees it; damage to a complete record is refused, not rolled back in silence.
steps: Create a task, update its title to 'second title', and move it to review with a result: confirmed records, whole, with newlines.
Copy the whole ledger, run the same title update through the service on the copy with title 'unconfirmed title', and take the one journal record that update added.
Append only the strict prefix of that record (half the line, no newline) to the original journal; the original export stays at the confirmed state.

Restart, read the row through the service (the confirmed row with status review), repeat the allowed update, close, reopen, then delete the export and the snapshot in a further copy and read the row rebuilt from the journal alone.
Make the change journal read-only, close a task in review, restore it: the call must not report success; the row stays review before and after the next successful update; no close entry is recorded.

On a fresh board, move a task to review, write the snapshot with the product's own writeSnapshot, damage a complete record that lies BEFORE the snapshot offset (newline kept), reopen and close: the close must refuse with TASK_JOURNAL_MISMATCH and change nothing on disk.
On another fresh board, damage the last complete record in the tail the same way and close: refused with TASK_JOURNAL_MISMATCH.
expected: The reopened service reads the confirmed row while the export is lagging; the repeated update succeeds, the close returns ok, reopening reads "third title" done, and a copy without the export and snapshot still reads it from the journal. A close whose append fails reports no success, the row stays review before AND after the next successful write, and no close is recorded. A complete record damaged in place is refused with TASK_JOURNAL_MISMATCH whether it lies in the tail or under the product's own snapshot, and the refused close changes nothing on disk.
failsWhen: An unconfirmed tail is presented as the confirmed row (or a damaged complete record is silently dropped), so the confirmed state is lost or a broken record passes.
trigger: A real update runs on a separate copy of the board; only half of its journal record reaches the original ledger, whose export stays at the confirmed state. The workspace restarts, reads the row through the service, repeats the allowed change, closes, and the derived files are removed to read the change back from the journal. Separately, one complete journal line is damaged in place.
oracle: REQ-294 and AC-2 in the analysis record taskboard-write-integrity: after an incomplete last write the last confirmed row is visible, a repeated allowed change is saved and reopening sees it.
realism: The interrupted write the analysis names: the row change and its verification data were two separate writes, so a process dying between them leaves an incomplete verification record. The orchestrator confirmed the realism of the criteria.

snapshot.title: A torn last record keeps the confirmed row and the next allowed change
snapshot.requirement: REQ-294: confirmed board changes survive an interrupted write and the close does not let manual edits through. AC-2: with an incomplete last record, after a restart the last confirmed row is visible; a repeated allowed change is saved and reopening sees it; damage to a complete record is not silently rolled back.
snapshot.expected: After the restart the last confirmed row is readable (title "second title"), the repeated update succeeds, the close returns ok, and a further read sees the row done with "third title".
steps: Create a task and update its title to 'second title' (a legal write).
Truncate the last line of the .dsh journal that recorded the task to half its bytes: the process died mid-append.
Start a second plugin instance on a copy of the ledger and read the row.
Repeat the allowed update with title 'third title'.
Close the task and read the row again from another copy of the ledger.
